statement: Guide covers land ranks (with database priority), night market point optimization, and efficient magic bean farming for the new farming update.
Night market becomes even more important as you scale up your farming.
Unlock land ranks in the night market as its sixth upgrade; needs a few magic beans, many crops unlocked, and decent evolution chance.
After unlocking land ranks, you automatically gain land rank experience whenever you harvest crops.
Rank boost is the eighth night market upgrade; requires mushrooms and gives more land rank experience per crop collected.
Land ranks are leveled by harvesting crops; handyman tools land ranks tab 'view experience' shows XP needed, and each plot ranks up individually (RNG).
Rank experience display is cluttered, he turns it off; plots differ in rank, and just keep growing crops to level them.
If one plot lags behind in rank, you can specifically harvest that plot.
Reset upgrades button shows a 7-day timer tied to weekly reset; you can respec land rank points only once per week.
Land rank database has 4 upgrades affecting the rest of account and 16 farming-related upgrades.
Points to spend come from total land ranks across all plots; 36 plots total if all unlocked.
You get one database point per total plot rank; available points visible by clicking any upgrade.
Evolution boost upgrades have diminishing returns per point and the four multiply together.
Balance points between the four evolution boosts, since the bottom one eventually gives less per point than upgrading the top one.
You need four points to get the four account bonuses; they unlock slowly as total plot rank rises.
Seed of stealth, first account bonus, gives 2% more stealth per farming level (58% for him) for all ninjas; great for sneaking masteries.
Seed of stealth is an amazing upgrade to help push sneaking masteries.
Seed of loot needs a few more ranks and gives 10% more drop rarity to all characters.
Seed of damage gives 20% more damage to all characters; needs a few hundred land ranks.
Last account bonus needs 3500 total land ranks and gives 5% boost to all stats on all characters.
Evolution boost category speeds unlocking new plants and evolutions, with four upgrades.
Evolution boost increases next crop chance by a percent per rank on the land plot; each plot differs by points and rank.
Evolution mega boost is a flat multiplier to evolution chance; you need other sources of evolution chance too.
e66 evolution chance is ideal to unlock all 140 crops (check evolution multiplier in farming); without it, last plots are a struggle.
He still has about 20% (possibly lower) chance to unlock last crop at his current evolution chance.
Evolution super boost gives more multiplicative evolution crop chance; Ultra boost is the fourth.
All four evolution boosts multiply, so spread decent points in each rather than dumping 1000 points into Ultra boost.
Production boost is hands down the best upgrade, though overgrowth or evolution chance may be more useful depending on stage.
Early game evolution chance is even more important than production boost.
In middle game production boost becomes your biggest upgrade, but you still need evolution and overgrowth chance.
Production boost caps at 100 times more crops per plant, four upgrades contribute; nothing more beyond that.
Production boost gives crops harvested a percent per plot rank; mega boost and super boost are flat multipliers, all multiply with product doubler.
He currently has product doubler at 195%, cannot give exact points needed to hit 100x.
Example to reach 100x at 120% doubler and rank 65: 125 production boost, 125 mega boost, 150 super boost points.
At 195% doubler and rank 100+ he needs far fewer production points to cap, freeing points, but he is at diminishing returns.
Don't overspend on the one weekly reset if you're about to gain many land ranks from harvesting.
Get to the 100x production cap, then move on to evolution chance and overgrowth chance.
Four farming experience boosts; soil exp boost gives experience based on land rank of the previous plot.
Don't micromanage putting highest-rank plot first for soil exp; better to upgrade all lands, difference is small (90% total at 200 points).
Soil exp mega boost gives flat farming exp (242 for him at rank 200); soil exp super boost gives a bigger flat rate.
Farmtastic super boost gives another bigger farming experience gain.
He only put 100 points in farmtastic super boost by oversight and will add another 100 to exceed exp super boost.
Overgrowth chance has three upgrades that multiply; 200 points in the first two gives him 145%.
Overgrowth mega boost gives 42%, third upgrade with 300 points gives 322; all three multiply so invest in each.
Even with huge overgrowth he has 0% chance at ranks 15-19ish, grows crops every 6 seconds, and reached 262x multiplier on some plants.
Biggest priority is evolution chance; he's at e65, giving only ~5% chance for the last crop.
e66 is the target for most people to unlock all 140 crops; this is first priority.
Production boost is second priority (or equal if enough points), giving more crops, night market bonuses, overgrowth and stats; just below evolution chance.
Third priority is overgrowth for crazy multipliers on products.
He basically guarantees x8, x16 is about 93%; guaranteed x32 possible with very high stats, harvesting every ~7 seconds with millions of beans.
Last priority is farming experience, but don't ignore it: farming level gives stealth and meal bonuses.
Unlock overgrowth in the night market as soon as you can with a few magic beans even if it means resetting early.
Overgrowth matters most if you can't check farming every hour or two; if you check hourly it's less valuable.
Evolution GMO breakpoint between 1.9 and 2 gives enough evolution chance to unlock all 160 crops.
Evolution chance comes from land rank upgrades, evolution GMO, alchemy and dinner menu meals; his magic number was 1.95 and he went to 2.
Speed GMO is the best early game upgrade and slightly better than OG fertilizer early.
Speed GMO gives growth speed per crop type you have at least 1000 of.
Speed GMO can give 6 second growth on glassy seeds and 1 second on apples late game.
OG fertilizer is the bean sink until end of time, can't be capped yet, but other upgrades are slightly higher priority.
Exp GMO is low priority early, a later game thing; caps at 100% with 100 upgrades and has a max button.
Unlock land ranks as soon as you can; it gives the most bonuses.
Value GMO is currently broken and gives little value to upgrade now; may be one of the best upgrades once fixed.
Super GMO is hands down the best farming upgrade but requires 100000 of each crop to work.
Early game don't invest beans in Super GMO as 100000 of each crop takes too long; better in mid and late game.
Start spending in Super GMO when you can reach 100000 of each crop in one growth cycle.
Earlier, use two passes: farm each crop to 1000 for speed GMO, then second pass to 100000 for Super GMO.
He waited to invest in Super GMO until he could get 100000 crops in under four hours; your timeframe may differ.
Super GMO caps at 25%, then no more beans needed; gives him 34.6x bonus to speed GMO, exp, evolution GMO and later value GMO.
Order: evolution chance to needed number first, then speed GMO up to 3%, 5%, then 9-10%.
Keep OG fertilizer cost similar to speed GMO until about 15% speed GMO, then mostly ignore OG fertilizer while upgrading Super GMO and speed GMO.
Basic method: leave crops grown, turn in all crops with crop tickets for beans, harvest again and turn in a second time.
His crops were worth 6 million beans on turn-in.
Do the bean turn-in on the highest evolution crop/seed for the most crops and beans.
Early game you can get a few thousand beans per turn-in giving progress in speed GMO and OG fertilizer.
Second tier needs decent overgrowth: turn in crops, then harvest just one plant (~20000 crops) and turn that in for more beans.
Drop only one crop on the ground at a time in the turn-in map in case of crash losing crop transfer tickets.
The process is slow but gets the most beans because of diminishing returns on magic beans.
Harvesting one plant gave 1.5 million beans; across all 36 plots could gain about 1.2 million more, varying with overgrowth.
Bean gain fluctuates with overgrowth chance and number of plants and land ranks; 64000x harvest gave 1.468 million beans.
Higher overgrowth multiplier gives more beans; harvesting a 262000x plant gave 2.9 million beans.
Harvesting a second plant before turning in only gave 600000 beans because diminishing returns scale badly.
Turn in one crop at a time; requires many crop tickets, so buy them every day.
Before bean turn-in, get everything to the last crop and let it grow 1 to 2 days early game for most overgrowth.
Turn in each crop individually; even 128x or 256x is much better than harvesting at x16 or x32, but give it time to overgrow.
Late game, harvesting one plant at a time would need 36-37 turn-in tickets, which is too many.
Guild method: turn in batches of 3-4 plants (one big, one or two small), using 4-6 tickets per turn-in every 2-3 days.
After reset, rebuild night market GMO stacks by sacrificing half your bean potential to keep the last 18 plants pregrown.
Before reset, harvest everything and do a final turn-in (another 6 million beans), then start over.
Use handyman tools to remove last-crop glassy seeds, plant first seed with plant all, then harvest pregrown last crops to jump start GMO stacks.
Harvesting 18 pregrown crops instantly gives 18 stacks, a 22x speed multiplier, making basic seeds grow in under a minute and restarting super and speed GMO.
Use the last 18 seeds you can, lock them in place and harvest; keep a few million of each in crop depot. Method isn't for everybody.
Late game apples grow too fast to lock; without a lock-all button you may need to lock initial crops to get enough 100K seeds for all 160 crops.
